member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.Codex.FishWikiImages
member.summary:
Maps fish (DT_Fish rows) to their image file names on abioticfactor.wiki.gg.
Researched 2026-06: each fish's wiki page (and the species table on /wiki/Fishing) uses the GAME'S ITEM ICON as the infobox image - file names like Itemicon_antefish.png or Item Icon - Gem Crab.png - NOT <PageName>.png. The names are too irregular to derive (mixed casing, rare01/rare_1 suffixes, internal names like FogFish for the Chordfish), so the tables below are curated.
Primary key is the DT_Fish ROW ID (e.g. Fogfish_rare1), because rare variants reuse their base species' display name in-game while the wiki gives each rare its own art (Oxidious/Osseous/Saxe/...). Display name is the fallback for future rows, then a best-effort guess in both wiki upload conventions.

member.summary: Display name -> wiki file, from the species table on /wiki/Fishing. Covers fish the row-id table may not know yet (newer game builds); note rare variants can't be resolved this way because they share the base display name.

member.summary: The verified row-id -> wiki-file table (for coverage tests).

member.summary: The verified display-name -> wiki-file table (for coverage tests).

member.name: P:AbioticEditor.Core.Codex.FishWikiImages.AllWikiFiles
member.summary: Every verified wiki File name across both tables, de-duplicated (rare variants and the row-id / display-name tables share many files). Used to pre-download the offline fallback bundle; the speculative guesses in are excluded.

member.summary: Wiki image file names to try, in order, for a DT_Fish row. The row id is authoritative (it distinguishes rare variants); the display name covers rows the id table doesn't know; the trailing guesses follow the two wiki upload conventions and simply resolve to no image when wrong.

member.summary: Wiki-sourced identity and lore for the DT_NPC_Traders rows (abioticfactor.wiki.gg/wiki/Trading + individual NPC pages). The game tables carry no display names - only row ids and portraits - so this reference data lives in Core where any frontend (editor UI, CLI, future web) can read it.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.Codex.TraderLore.Entry
member.param: Display name.
Where you first meet them.
Short lore.

How/when they actually become a trader. The game's DT_NPC_Traders table carries no world-flag gate for most of them (you unlock them by meeting/helping them in the world or by finishing the story), so the editor cannot infer this from flags - it is curated here so the UI never wrongly claims a trader is "available from the start".

When set, the spoiler system treats this trader as future content unless the world has this flag. Required for traders whose DT_NPC_Traders row carries no RequiredWorldFlags even though they are NOT available from the start (the game gates them via NPC encounter events or story completion instead of a save flag, so is empty and the normal availability check would always pass).

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.Items.BackpackSpecialSlotCatalog
member.summary:
Which backpack inventory indices are special (refrigerated / freezer / shielded / warmer), keyed by backpack item id. Indices are 0-based into Inventory_.
The game wires this via DT_ItemCosmetics (row name = item id) -> DataAsset_51_* (ObjectProperty) -> an InventoryData_Parent_C data asset carrying per-type slot-index arrays (see docs/research-backpack-traits.md). walks that chain at runtime so backpacks added by future game versions are picked up without an editor change; is the table verified against the current build, used when game assets aren't available.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.Items.ItemCatalog.RelinkLocalizedText(AbioticEditor.Core.Items.ItemCatalogEntry,CUE4Parse.UE4.Assets.Objects.FStructFallback)
member.summary: Rewrites 's display name/description from the given supplemental-table row, leaving every other field untouched.
member.remarks: ItemTable_Global's row FText gets re-baked at cook time under a fresh namespace/key that Abiotic Factor's shipped locres files never cover - confirmed by a live probe against the installed game: with a non-English culture loaded, 0 of 1545 ItemTable_Global item names differed from their English source string. The per-category supplemental table this same row was originally authored in (e.g. ItemTable_Gear, ItemTable_Weapons) keeps the row's real namespace/key, which the locres does cover. The two copies' ItemName_/ItemDescription_ source text is byte-identical in English, so preferring the supplemental copy is a no-op under English and a real translation under any other loaded culture.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.SkillCatalog
member.summary:
The ordered list of player skills plus level/XP math.
Player saves store skills positionally: the Skills_ array in CharacterSaveData carries one Abiotic_CharacterSkill_Struct per skill, and every entry's SkillName field is the compiler default (skill_sprinting) - identity comes from array order alone.
The array is serialized in the game's on-screen skill order (the Fitness / Combat / Survival grouping of the in-game skills panel), NOT DT_Skills row order. The two orders differ: DT_Skills lists Accuracy second and Strength near the end, but the game writes Strength second (Fitness) and Accuracy in the Combat group, so a catalog keyed to DT_Skills mislabels every skill that moves between the two orders. The earlier "verified against an end-game save" check could not catch this: in a fully maxed save every position reads ~91,655 XP, so any ordering looks correct. The canonical order below is the in-game panel order (see ); identity is the array index. Source: abioticfactor.wiki.gg/wiki/Skills.

member.name: F:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.SkillCatalog.CanonicalOrder
member.summary: The in-game skill-panel order (Fitness, then Combat, then Survival) by DT_Skills row name. This is the order the game serializes the positional Skills_ array, so it is the single source of truth for index -> skill identity, used by both and .

member.name: F:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.SkillCatalog.XpThresholds
member.summary: Cumulative XP required to reach each level. Index 0 = level 1 (200 XP) ... index 19 = level 20 (91,655 XP). Source: abioticfactor.wiki.gg/wiki/Skills (v1.0), confirmed against capped end-game save values.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.SkillCatalog.LevelForXp(System.Double)
member.summary: Level reached at (0 when below the level-1 threshold).

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.SkillCatalog.XpForLevel(System.Int32)
member.summary: Minimum cumulative XP for (0 for level 0).

member.name: P:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.SkillCatalog.Fallback
member.summary: Built-in skill table (DT_Skills order, DONOTUSE rows removed). Used when the game assets aren't available; supersedes it when they are.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.SkillCatalog.WithUnknownPlaceholders(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.SkillDefinition},System.Int32)
member.summary: Pads with "Unknown skill #N" placeholders so a save whose positional Skills_ array is LONGER than the known catalog (newer game version added a skill) still shows - and round-trips - every entry. Returns unchanged when nothing is missing.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.SkillCatalog.LoadFrom(AbioticEditor.Core.Assets.GameAssetProvider)
member.summary: Loads skill display metadata (name, description, icon) from the game's DT_Skills DataTable and arranges it in the save's positional order (, the in-game panel order), skipping rows whose display name carries the DONOTUSE marker. Returns when mappings are missing or the table can't be read.
member.remarks: Skills are positional (identity = index in the save's Skills_ array). That order is the in-game panel order, which is NOT the same as DT_Skills row order, so the table is used only for per-skill text/icons and is re-sequenced into . Rows the canonical order doesn't name (a mod or a newer game version that added a skill) are appended after the known ones in DT_Skills row order - a best-effort guess, since their true save position is unknown. A save whose array is longer than the catalog still round-trips safely via .

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerIdentifier
member.summary: Helpers for the opaque player identifier that names a player save (Player_<id>.sav) and fills its top-level SaveIdentifier property. On Steam this is a 17-digit SteamID64; on Game Pass / Microsoft Store / Epic and other non-Steam copies it is some other account token. The editor treats the id as an opaque string and never assumes it is numeric; is the single gate for the Steam-only extras (persona lookup, achievements).

member.name: F:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerIdentifier.MaxLength
member.summary: Maximum identifier length we accept in a file name. A SteamID64 is 17 chars; this is generous headroom for a GUID-style or platform token without risking a path limit.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerIdentifier.IsSteamId(System.String)
member.summary: True for a 17-digit public-range SteamID64 (same shape as the Steam loginusers.vdf persona regex). Used to gate Steam-only features; everything else is treated as a valid non-Steam id.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerIdentifier.IsSafeFileToken(System.String)
member.summary: True when is safe to use as the Player_<id>.sav file-name component: non-empty, within , only letters, digits, -, _ or . (no path separators, drive colons, wildcards or control chars), not a bare dot run and not a Windows reserved device name. This is the single place to relax if a real platform id needs other characters.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerIdentifier.TryParseFromPlayerFileName(System.String,System.String@)
member.summary: Extracts the id from a Player_<id>.sav path. Returns false (and an empty id) when the file name does not carry the prefix. The id is returned verbatim, opaque - no numeric assumption. Consolidates the formerly-duplicated file-name parsers.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerIdentifier.TryParseSteamId(System.String,System.UInt64@)
member.summary: Parses as a numeric SteamID64 for the Steam-only paths that need the number (achievements, vdf lookup). Returns false for any non-Steam id.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerIdentifier.SteamIdRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^7656119\\d{10}$
Options:
RegexOptions.CultureInvariant
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match the string "7656119".
○ Match a Unicode digit exactly 10 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerIdentifier.SafeTokenRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$
Options:
RegexOptions.CultureInvariant
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [\-.0-9A-Z_a-z] atomically at least once.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerSaveFactory
member.summary:
Builds new player saves: a reset-to-blank routine, a bundled-template builder and the create-from-template path the editor's "add player" flow uses.
Abiotic Factor has no documented "make a fresh character save" API we can call, and the file is a delta-serialized blueprint tree, so a brand-new player is fabricated from an existing save's structure with every progression field reset. The reset reuses so it stays in lock-step with how the editor writes saves.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerSaveFactory.ResetToBlank(AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerSaveData)
member.summary: Resets in place to a fresh-character baseline: full vitals and limb health, zero money, all skills back to 0 XP, every unlock/compendium/kill list emptied and every inventory slot cleared. The save's structural shape (array lengths, skill positions) is preserved - only values change. Does not write to disk.

member.summary: Reads the player save at , resets it to a blank character and returns the serialized bytes with a neutral (empty) owner identifier. Used once to generate the bundled blank-player-template.sav asset.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerSaveFactory.CreateFromTemplate(System.Byte[],System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Creates a new Player_<id>.sav in from the blank-template , stamping the new owner's SaveIdentifier. Returns the new file's path.

Parses an Abiotic Factor Player_*.sav file into typed models.
AF property names carry hash-suffixed signatures from the blueprint compiler - e.g. Hunger_2_A6C5CC6E41993323B119FA9E0B3894CA. We match by prefix so the reader is resilient to suffix changes between game patches.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerSaveWriter
member.summary: Applies mutations to the underlying tree of a . The save then re-serializes byte-perfect except for the edited fields.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerSaveWriter.FullNames
member.summary:
Full hash-suffixed blueprint property names, harvested from fixture saves.
Abiotic Factor delta-serializes saves: any property still at its blueprint default is omitted entirely (e.g. a fresh character has no Hunger_ tag inside CurrentSurvivalStats_ because hunger is still at the full 100). To write such a stat the missing must be created, and that requires the exact full name - the hash suffix is part of the name the game looks up. These suffixes are emitted by the blueprint compiler and are stable across game patches (verified identical between build -2146453646 and -2146453647 saves).

member.summary: Patches the positional Skills_ array from . Skills are matched by array index; only CurrentSkillXP_ and CurrentXPMultiplier_ are written (the SkillName text fields are inert blueprint defaults the game ignores). Both fields sit at their blueprint default (0 XP, 1.0 multiplier) on an untouched skill and can be omitted from the save, so both use create-on-miss (see ). Out-of-range entries are skipped.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerSaveWriter.ApplyTraits(AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerSaveData,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.String})
member.summary: Replaces the Traits_ name array with (internal row names like Trait_LeadBelly). Mirrors the WorldFlags writer: an existing ArrayProperty instance is kept, only its element buffer is swapped. Unlike WorldFlags, a missing tag is created (see ): a character that started with no traits never gets a Traits_ tag at all, so a plain prefix lookup would silently no-op on every trait added to such a character.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.InventoryGift
member.summary: Places a single item into an already-loaded 's inventory, choosing the first free backpack (main) slot and falling back to the hotbar. Used by cross-save transfers (e.g. moving an item out of a world container into a player save). Mutates the player model via ; the caller writes the save afterwards (which keeps a .bak). The source is never touched here - the caller removes it after a successful add so the move stays a move, not a copy.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerRespawnRevert
member.summary: Moves every player's respawn/load-in point back to a story chapter's punch-card terminal - the position counterpart of a story rewind. resets quest state but never touches where a player loads back in, which could otherwise leave them standing somewhere the reverted story hasn't reached yet. Only X/Y/Z and the terminal id are touched - the same fields changed by picking a terminal (without also picking a different streamed sub-level) in the PLAYER > SPAWN tab; LastSafeWorldGUID_ is left as-is, since that tab already treats the two as independently editable.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.PlayerSaves.PlayerSaveIdentity
member.summary: Player identity surgery. A player's owner id lives in TWO places: the file name (Player_<id>.sav) AND the top-level SaveIdentifier StrProperty inside the save (see dotnet/docs/research-slot-types.md, Q3). Renaming the file alone leaves the content claiming the old owner, so both are rewritten together. The id is an opaque string (a SteamID64 on Steam, an account token on Game Pass / Epic / non-Steam); the historical method names keep the "SteamId" wording. The ulong overloads forward to the string ones for callers that still hold a numeric SteamID64.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.BenchUpgradeCatalog
member.summary:
The bench upgrade modules the game lets a player install on a crafting / cooking / ammo bench. In the save these are not a numeric tier - each installed module is a gameplay tag (BenchUpgrade.<Row>) inside the bench deployable's ChangableData_.GameplayTags_ container (note the in-game misspelling "Changable").
Read/write helpers here operate on a single DeployedObjectMap entry's struct property list and mutate the gameplay-tag list in place, so the writer re-serializes the rest of the save byte-perfect. Untouched tag strings are preserved exactly (some saves store the bare row, others the fully-qualified tag), so we only ever append the canonical form for a newly-installed module and remove by matching the row.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.ContainmentDynamicSlots
member.summary:
The EDynamicProperty slots a deployed Leyak Containment Unit uses on its item data (ChangableData_.DynamicProperties_).
The blueprint reaches these through generic Get/SetDynamicProperty calls, so the slot names are not recoverable from the cooked asset; they were pinned down from the saves instead. Across every fixture world, Generic2 and Generic3 are used by no other deployable class at all, Generic1 only ever holds 0..100 (matching the blueprint's MaxStability of 100 and its -14/night decay), and Generic3 matches the creature the metadata save assigns to that exact unit in every case observed (0 for each Leyak unit, 1 for each Krasue unit), which is also the order of the blueprint's two-entry LeyakContainmentData array.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.DoorClassCatalog
member.summary:
Curated catalog of every door blueprint class observed in AF world saves so far. Built by surveying the 42 WorldSave_*.sav fixtures across the game's maps plus inspecting AbioticFactor/Content/Blueprints/Doors/ blueprints in the paks (see DoorProbeTests).
Lock kinds are best-effort labels derived from the blueprint family - full blueprint K2Node inspection would be needed to resolve specific keycards or part requirements per instance.
No class is labelled Flag: whether a door is story-controlled is set per placed instance, never by the class, and a survey of all 77 cooked sub-levels found only 11 doors in the whole game that carry one. Labelling a class "story controlled" therefore mislabelled hundreds of ordinary doors. reads the real per-door gate from the level files and names the flag; UIs should let that override the class default.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.DoorWikiImageCatalog
member.summary:
Maps door blueprint classes (see ) to image file names on abioticfactor.wiki.gg, for the door detail panel.
Researched 2026-06: the wiki has NO articles for door types (no Security Door, Blast Door, Hatch, Doors or Keycard(s) pages) and only two files with "door" in the title on the entire wiki - Pet Rock - Door.png (a pet rock posed at a door) and Aim Icon - Door.png (the 64px interaction glyph). File-namespace searches for security/blast/hatch/shutter/vacuum/keycard/gatekey imagery only return item icons and sector maps. In short: door types simply are not pictured on the wiki, so this catalog is an honest near-empty subset; unmapped classes keep the sector-card fallback in the UI with a "no door image available" caption.
The one defensible mapping: the Tram page's photo for the tram rail door (the image shows the tram vehicle the rail door belongs to).

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.PetCatalog
member.summary:
Reference data for the pet system: the family/variant catalog and the XP->level curve.
Three sources layer together, most authoritative first: 1. - the game's own DT_Pets/DT_NPCList tables (see ), applied process-wide once paks are mounted. New companions the game adds appear with no editor change at all. 2. Pak class enumeration in - catches modded NPC classes that merely look like a known family. 3. The curated table below - friendly names, categories, and a working offline fallback when no game install is available.
Pets are level 0-20; level is derived from a cumulative-XP curve fit to the two values the wiki publishes (level 1 = 4 XP, level 20 = 750 XP). The stored XP integer is the source of truth; the level is a derived label.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.PetCatalog.BuildVariants(AbioticEditor.Core.Assets.GameAssetProvider)

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.PetItemCatalog
member.summary:
The inventory-item side of the pet system: pet items carried in a player's hotbar / Companion slot. A carried pet is an ordinary item row tagged Item.Pet, with health in CurrentItemDurability_ and XP / mutation in DynamicProperties_ (see ). This catalog bridges those item rows to the world creature classes in so a pet can be moved between a world save (PetNPC) and a player save (hotbar item).
When the game paks are mounted (), the item list and the item<->creature bridge come straight from the game's Item.Pet rows and DT_Pets/DT_NPCList, so pets added by future updates work with no code change. The curated table below is the offline fallback.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.QuestFlagDependencies
member.summary:
Curated per-quest flag dependencies that the coarse chapter model ('s linear chapter triggers + region-opening chapters) does not capture. A flag here requires the listed flags to be set first, so the editor can offer to flip a whole quest's granular steps instead of leaving a half-finished state (the classic symptom: a quest's "completed" flag is set but its "started" flag isn't, so the in-game door/NPC the step controls never resolves).
This same graph, walked in reverse by , is also how a story rewind () knows which granular flags to clear alongside a chapter trigger: without it, rewinding past a chapter only cleared the 37 curated trigger flags and left every granular step (and, at the very end, End_MainStoryComplete itself) still set, so the game kept treating the save as finished.
Deliberately conservative: only steps that are definitionally true (you cannot COMPLETE a quest you never STARTED) or confirmed from the wiki walkthrough / real completed-save flag dumps are listed, so setting a flag can never fabricate an inconsistent world. Covers the full main story spine from Office through the finale - records the physical results (doors opened, NPCs killed) of a step for tools that can apply them.

member.summary: The physical world-state a completed quest step leaves behind, for tools that apply consequences (open doors / mark NPCs dead). NPC and door entries are matched by the in-save actor's class/marker, since the exact GUID is per-save.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.WorldAreaCatalog
member.summary:
Turns a region/level token (parsed from a world-save file name or an actor's SoftObjectPath) into a friendly in-game area name, e.g. Facility_MFWest → "Manufacturing West", WorldSave_Facility_Office1 → "The Office Sector".
This is a best-effort label, not an authoritative coordinate lookup: the game does not store a coordinate-to-area mapping in the save, so the area is inferred from the level the actor/save belongs to. Tokens we recognise get a curated name (aligned with the teleporter region names in ); everything else is prettified (strip the Facility_ prefix, split underscores) so a new level still reads sensibly rather than showing a raw path.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.PetHealth
member.summary: Shared pet health logic for the CLI and App. The save's CurrentHealthMap_ records only the current per-limb value - the blueprint maximum is not in the save - so "full" is treated as the pet's strongest current limb. Creatures only use a subset of limbs (e.g. a pest tracks the head; its other limbs sit at 0), so edits only touch limbs that are already non-zero ("tracked") and never enable a limb the creature doesn't use.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.WorldDeployable.ParseClaim(System.String)
member.summary: Parses a bed-claim string of the form <ownerId>}|!|{<name>. Returns (null, null) when has no separator or the halves are empty (unclaimed bed). The owner id is opaque (not assumed numeric). Some player names in the fixture saves carry invisible private-use-area glyphs (e.g. U+E110 wrapping the name - Steam/in-game styling artifacts); those are stripped so the name compares and displays cleanly.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.WorldContainmentUnit
member.summary:
One deployed Leyak Containment Unit, wherever it stands in the world.
A unit is an ordinary player-placed deployable () living in a region save's DeployedObjectMap, keyed by a GUID. Whether it currently holds a creature is not stored on the unit: the metadata save's LeyakContainmentIDs map (creature row -> unit GUID) is the link, which is why an empty unit is simply one whose GUID no entry points at. The unit does keep its own copy of which creature it holds, as the LeyakContainmentData index in EDynamicProperty::Generic3, and its containment stability (0..100) in EDynamicProperty::Generic1.
member.param: The DeployedObjectMap GUID; the value side of a LeyakContainmentIDs entry.
File name of the region save the unit was found in (e.g. WorldSave_Facility.sav). Empty when read from a single save in isolation.
World X of the unit.
World Y of the unit.
World Z of the unit.
The unit's stored stability, or null when the unit carries no Generic1 slot.
The unit's own Generic3 index, or null when it carries no such slot. -1 is possible on a save that stored an out-of-range value.
The creature row the metadata save assigns to this unit, or null when the unit is empty. Filled in by , not by the reader.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.WorldDoorKind
member.summary:
Which door map a came from. The two maps store significantly different fields:
- SimpleDoorMap, with an enum state, a yaw rotation, and a one-way-unlocked flag.
- SecurityDoorMap, just a single IsDoorOpen bool.
Both kinds also carry a NoReset bool.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.WorldDoor
member.summary:
A single door entry from a world save. Backs onto either SimpleDoorMap or SecurityDoorMap. The two underlying structs are different, so some fields are null depending on :
Simple doors populate , , , and .
Security doors populate and .
member.param: Map key - an actor path string like /Game/Maps/Facility.Facility:PersistentLevel.SimpleDoor_ParentBP_C_0.
Which underlying map this door lives in.
Simple-door enum value (e.g. E_DoorStates::NewEnumerator0). Stored as the enum string because ByteProperty deserializes large-form enums as FString. null for security doors.
Simple-door rotation (in degrees, sometimes negative). null for security doors.
true if a simple one-way door has been opened from the locked side. null for security doors.
true if a security door is currently open. null for simple doors.
If true, this door is exempted from session-restart resets. Present on both kinds.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.PetDynamicProperties
member.summary: Builds and patches DynamicProperties_ arrays (the {Key:EDynamicProperty, Value:int} struct arrays carrying a pet's XP / mutation, on inventory-item slots). Fabricating these from scratch fails on reload because UE5.4 stores the enum type in the property tag's complete-type-name parameters AND struct arrays carry an internal prototype. The verified trick: reuse an existing element's tag objects for new elements, and - when a slot has no array at all - graft a detached clone of an existing array tag (whose prototype is intact) rather than constructing one. All DynamicProperties_ use the same EDynamicProperty enum, so any element is a valid template.

member.summary:
Adds a pet to the world's PetNPC map by cloning an existing entry (so the struct layout is byte-identical to what the game writes) and overwriting only the fields that define this pet: a fresh GUID key, class, name, health, XP, and location. When a pet of the same class already exists it is preferred as the clone template (so the limb set matches). (e.g. a carried pet's durability) is distributed across the template's limbs to keep the total HP; null fills every limb. Returns the new GUID, or null when the world has no creature at all to use as a template. Mirrors .
When the world has no pets yet, the entry is cloned from a story NPC instead: the PetNPC and NarrativeNPCMap maps share the same NPC-state struct, so a pet can be placed into a world that has never had one, as long as it contains some creature.

member.param: False when the pet's XP could not be carried across, which happens when the entry had to be cloned from a story NPC: a pet keeps its XP in a dynamic-property list that story NPCs simply do not have, and there is nothing in such a world to copy that list's shape from. The pet still arrives, with its name, kind, place and health - it just starts at level one. Callers that promise the level survives must check this before saying so.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.WorldSaveWriter.FindOrCreatePetMap(UeSaveGame.SaveGame)
member.summary: The save's PetNPC map, created empty when the world has never held a pet.

remarks.para: A region the player has never taken a companion into simply has no such map: the game delta-serializes, and a map still at its blueprint default is left out of the file entirely. In practice only WorldSave_Facility.sav ships one, so refusing to create it meant a pet could only ever be sent to the main facility.

The new map is built from NarrativeNPCMap's own tag rather than assembled from scratch, because that tag already carries the exact key and value type names the game wrote, and the two maps hold the same NPC-state struct. Copying them is what makes the created map serialize identically to one the game would have written. Returns null when there is no NPC map to copy the shape from - a world with no creature of any kind, which is also a world with nothing to clone an entry from.

member.summary:
Re-homes every claim held by in DeployedObjectMap to and returns how many were rewritten. Everything from the separator onwards is carried over untouched, so the claimer's name survives exactly - including the invisible private-use glyphs some in-game names wrap themselves in, which the display path strips but the file must keep.
Only a text that starts with <oldOwnerId>}|!|{ counts. The game reuses the same separator as the line break in sign text, so a hand-typed sign reading "Stolas}|!|{castle" is two lines rather than a claim by a player called Stolas, and a match anywhere in the middle of a string is somebody's typing, not an ownership record.
This is the different-length-safe half of an owner-id change: because the save is re-serialized afterwards, the FString length prefixes are recomputed and the ids do not have to be the same size. See for the byte-level fast path used when they are.

member.summary:
Maps a world-state feature (by ) to candidate abioticfactor.wiki.gg image file names, so a feature tab can show one representative picture of that structure type. The image is per type (every tram shares the tram image).
Mapped structures: the Teleporter Pad (/wiki/Teleporter_Pad), the Tram (/wiki/Tram), and the Power Socket (the Energy page's Outlet.png render). Elevators have no dedicated wiki render and the lever/keypad icons misrepresent them, so they show no image rather than a misleading one. The remaining fixed world-state structures (buttons, fixed world teleporters, triggers) have no wiki render - "Teleporter"/"Power" are disambiguation pages, buttons appear only in walkthrough prose, and triggers are invisible logic volumes - so they map to nothing and the feature tab simply shows no image. member.summary:
Editor for NPCSpawnMap (region saves): each NPC spawner actor stores its cooldown state, spawn count, and encounter flags. Editing these fields lets a player reset spawner cooldowns or manipulate spawn counts without waiting for the in-game cooldown to expire.
Each entry value is a StructProperty → PropertiesStruct with the following editable leaves (blueprint-hash suffix is matched by prefix):
CurrentCooldownRemaining_Seconds until this spawner can fire again (DoubleProperty). Set to 0 to allow an immediate spawn.
LastDayOnCooldown_Game day when the cooldown was last set (IntProperty).
SpawnCount_Total number of times this spawner has spawned (IntProperty).
HasSpawnedOnce_Whether this spawner has ever fired (BoolProperty).
MinutesPassedCooldownStarted_In-game minutes elapsed when the current cooldown started (IntProperty).
HasBeenEncounteredOnce_Whether the player has ever encountered this spawner's NPC (BoolProperty).

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.Features.PortalMapFeature
member.summary:
Editor for PortalMap (region saves): each entry is a world teleporter actor (BP_Teleporter_ParentBP_C_*, the fixed teleporter pads found on the ground across maps) whose persisted state is stored in a SaveData_PortalStruct. In every save inspected the struct carries exactly two leaves:
ActorPath_ (SoftObjectPath) - the actor's own path; read-only and already encoded in the entry key, so it is not surfaced as a field.
PortalActive_ (BoolProperty) - whether this teleporter pad has been activated/unlocked. This is the one editable value, exposed here as active.
On the teleporter "tag"/linking the user asked about: the linking that pairs teleporters is not stored in the PortalMap struct - there is no tag, channel, frequency, or group leaf inside SaveData_PortalStruct (verified across the Facility, Salem, Train and Cabin region saves: only ActorPath_ + PortalActive_ are ever present). World teleporter pads are static blueprints whose destinations are baked into the level, so the save only persists their activated state. Player-placed teleporter networking lives in DeployedObjectMap instead, encoded in the deployable's PlayerMadeString_ (the }|!|{-separated name format, same scheme documented for benches/personal teleporters), with an (empty in observed saves) GameplayTags_ GameplayTagContainer on the same deployable. No discoverable built-in catalogue of allowed teleporter tags exists in the saves or modeled tables, so a constrained WorldMapField.Choice "tag" field is intentionally not exposed here; wiring it would belong on a DeployedObjectMap feature once a sourced tag vocabulary is found.
Implementation mirrors : derive from , expose one typed bool field, and patch the single leaf in via .

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.Features.ServerEntitlementsFeature
member.summary:
Editor for ServerEntitlements (the metadata save): the per-player ownership entitlements list, keyed by a player's SteamID64. Each entry value is a StructProperty -> PropertiesStruct with one member, Entitlements (an of strings) - e.g. EarlyAccess, SupportersEdition.
Rather than a single comma-separated text blob, every known entitlement is shown as its own on/off toggle so the player can see all available grants at a glance; any entitlement already present that this build doesn't recognise is shown as an extra toggle too, so nothing is hidden or lost. The SteamID key is resolved to the player's Steam persona name where known.
The list (EarlyAccess, SupportersEdition) covers every ownership entitlement seen across the test fixtures; new ones still surface and round-trip via the dynamic "extra toggle" path above, so the editor never silently drops one. NOTE: the metadata save also carries a sibling map, UserEntitlements, keyed the same way but holding the player's recipe entitlements (hundreds of recipe_* tokens). member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.Features.TeleporterPadFeature
member.summary:
Editor for player-placed Teleporter Pads (Deployed_TeleporterPad_C entries in DeployedObjectMap). A pad's "tag" - the identifier that links it into a teleporter network with every other pad sharing the same tag - is stored as an integer TeleporterFrequency inside the deployable's ChangableData_ → DynamicProperties_ array. This feature exposes that as a constrained tag choice (the 134 built-in tags from ) plus the raw frequency integer for exact control. Two pads set to the same tag link together.
Implemented directly against (not the simple ) because it filters DeployedObjectMap to just the pad class and reaches into a nested dynamic-property array rather than top-level leaves.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.Features.TeleporterTagCatalog
member.summary:
The built-in Teleporter Pad "tags" (a.k.a. frequencies) the game lets a player pick from to link pads together - two pads on the same tag form a network. A pad stores its choice as an integer TeleporterFrequency dynamic property: 0 = unassigned, and 1..133 = the 133 named tags below (134 selectable values in total, matching the wiki's count).
Order is the in-game frequency index, recovered from the Teleporter Pad wiki table read column-major (its columns are coherent groups: NATO A-M, NATO N-Z, region names, damage types, …) and verified against real save data - every tagged pad in the test fixtures resolves to a sensible region name (27→Facility, 34→The Reactors, 122→Far Garden, 133→Voussoir). If a future patch reorders the list, only this array needs updating.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.Features.TramMapFeature
member.summary:
Editor for TramMap (region saves; in practice only WorldSave_Facility.sav): each tram actor stores the station it last parked at plus any on-board container inventories. The last-parked station is editable; the on-board inventory count is shown read-only.
Editing the last station. LastStation_ is a SoftObjectPath whose station identity lives in its SubPathString (e.g. PersistentLevel.TramSystem_Station_C_9); its PackageName/AssetName are the constant /Game/Maps/Facility + Facility for every tram, so the AssetName carries no per-tram information. Rather than let the user type an arbitrary (and easily invalid) path, this feature collects the set of stations the save actually references - the SubPathString of every tram's current LastStation_ - and offers those as an editable choice. Writing a chosen value only replaces the SubPathString leaf (PackageName/AssetName stay untouched) via .
Known limitation: the option set is the union of stations currently occupied by some tram. Because each tram is parked at a distinct station, this lists only stations that at least one tram is sitting at right now - it cannot enumerate empty stations the level defines but no tram currently occupies (that would require reading the level asset, not the save). In practice the facility's trams cover the reachable stations, so this is enough to re-park a tram at any station another tram has visited.
Schema: map key = tram actor path (e.g. /Game/Maps/Facility…Tram_ParentBP_C_0); value = StructProperty → PropertiesStruct with the following leaves:
ActorPath_ (StructProperty SoftObjectPath) – tram actor path; mirrors the map key and is skipped (the key already identifies the tram).
LastStation_ (StructProperty SoftObjectPath) – station the tram last parked at; the editable value is the SubPathString component.
ContainerInventories_ (ArrayProperty of Struct) – on-board storage; surfaced as a read-only inventory count.

member.summary:
Editor for TriggerMap (region saves): each entry represents a named scripted world trigger and records how many times it has fired during the current playthrough. Setting TimesTriggered to zero effectively "resets" a trigger so that its scripted event can fire again on the next qualifying occurrence.
The only editable field is timesTriggered (int). triggerId is surfaced as a read-only display string because it is identical to the map entry key and editing it would create an inconsistency that Abiotic Factor would likely ignore or reject.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.Features.VehicleMapFeature
member.summary:
Editor for VehicleMap (region saves): each spawned vehicle actor stores whether it is currently driveable and whether it has been destroyed. The two editable booleans let a player restore a wrecked vehicle or prevent a vehicle from being driven without physically moving it.
Read-only display fields expose the vehicle's blueprint class, its persistent ID string, and how many on-board container inventories it carries.
Schema: map key = actor spawn path (e.g. /Game/Maps/Facility_MFWest...VehicleSpawn_Forklift_C_3); value = StructProperty → PropertiesStruct with the following leaves:
Class_ (SoftObjectProperty) – vehicle blueprint class path.
VehicleID_ (StrProperty) – stable runtime ID string.
Transform_ (StructProperty Transform) – world transform (read-only).
ContainerInventories_ (ArrayProperty) – on-board storage slots.
VehicleDriveable_ (BoolProperty) – whether the vehicle can be driven.
VehicleDestroyed_ (BoolProperty) – whether the vehicle is wrecked.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.ContainmentSurvey
member.summary:
The world-wide picture of Leyak containment, assembled from two places that have to be read together:
the metadata save's LeyakContainmentIDs map - creature row -> unit GUID, the only record of which unit holds a creature (and, being keyed by creature, proof that a creature can be in at most one unit at a time);
each region save's DeployedObjectMap - the units themselves, occupied or not. Units are player-deployed only (no cooked level places one), so this is the complete set.
In every fixture world every unit sits in WorldSave_Facility.sav, but nothing stops a player carrying one into another region, so the scan covers every sibling region save.
member.param: Every deployed containment unit found, occupied ones carrying the creature the metadata save assigns them.
Creature -> unit GUID entries whose unit was not found in any region save (a unit destroyed outside the game's own release path, or a region save that could not be read).
File names of sibling saves that failed to parse, so a caller can say the survey may be incomplete instead of quietly under-reporting.

The save records door STATE only, and can only guess a lock kind per blueprint class - which over-reports "story controlled", because the standard hinged door class CAN be gated but almost never is. member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.FlagGate
member.summary: Prerequisite model for world flags. Two rules: 1. Story trigger flags (DT_StoryProgression) are strictly linear - every earlier chapter's trigger must be set first. 2. Ordinary flags belong to a region (area prefix); the region only becomes reachable at a specific story chapter, so that chapter's trigger flag is a prerequisite (e.g. no Labs flag makes sense before Labs_MiddleProgression's predecessors fired). Areas with no story mapping (anomaly portals like NightRealm, account-level metas) are left ungated.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.FlagGate.DependentsOf(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.String},System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.String})
member.summary: Every currently-set flag that (directly or transitively, per ) required one of - the granular counterpart of clearing a chapter trigger. A story rewind that only removes the 37 curated trigger flags leaves every quest step built on top of them still set, so the game keeps reading the world as further along than the rewound chapter; this closes that gap by pulling in the whole dependent chain.

member.summary: Every currently-set flag whose region opens strictly after (per 's area-to-chapter gate), regardless of whether it is wired into the curated graph. That graph deliberately omits any-order steps within a region (the Dams pumps, the three Hydroplant survivors, the Security gates - see the comment on ), so alone never clears them: rewinding past a region that was reached out of sequence (e.g. via a tram/teleporter shortcut) would otherwise leave those flags set and the game would keep reading the world as having reached it.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.SectorMapCalibration
member.summary:
Projects world coordinates onto the game's drawn sector maps, so a door can be pinned on the map a player recognises from the pamphlet they picked up in-game.
The game stores NO world bounds for these drawings - DT_MapPamphlets holds only a sector, a level handle, an image and a strip flag - and the game never draws a "you are here" marker on them, so there is nothing to read. Each fit below was solved offline by SectorMapCalibrationProbe.Solve_Fits, which rasterises the drawn floor plan and searches orientation, scale and offset for the placement that lands the most of the level's actor cloud on the plan, then checked by eye against labelled landmarks (restrooms, lifts, vending machines) on the drawing.
A level absent from has no usable sector map and callers must fall back to a plain relative plot. That covers most of the game, for three separate reasons:
Only 11 pamphlets exist for 77 cooked sub-levels.
Three of those drawings are useless - Secure Area reads "SITE MAP UNAVAILABLE FOR SECURITY PURPOSES" and has no floor plan at all, Residence is a washed-out blank (the game's own asset is even named "Map_ResidenceTerribleMap"), and the game ships Map_Containment pointing at the Office Level 1 artwork.
Office Level 2 and the Dam refused to settle: every orientation scored within a few percent of every other, and none put those levels' restrooms and lifts where the drawing labels them. A pin that is confidently wrong is worse than no pin, so they are left out.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.StoryFlagSync
member.summary: Cross-file helper: when the metadata save's story chapter is set, the matching trigger flags live in the sibling WorldSave_Facility.sav (the main level). This adds every missing trigger flag up to a chapter - additive only, with the standard pre-write backup.
member.remarks: Each operation comes in two halves. The Plan* methods take an already-read save and work out the new flag list, touching no files; the methods named after them read the sibling save, apply the plan and write it back. The split exists because the browser build has no local file system to walk - it hands the bytes in itself - and because it makes the flag rules testable without a save on disk.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.WorldSteamIdPatcher
member.summary:
Rewrites bed-claim owner ids inside world saves when a player's owner id changes. Claims are stored as <ownerId>}|!|{<name> in deployable CustomTextDisplay_ strings, and the editor takes one of two routes depending on whether the ids are the same length.
Same length (always true for two SteamID64s): an in-place, same-length byte replacement. Every other byte of the file stays identical, which keeps the round-trip guarantee without re-serializing the save at all. Strings appear as ASCII or UTF-16LE depending on the claimer's name; both encodings are scanned.
Different length (an Xbox account id is 16 digits against a SteamID64's 17, so every Game Pass conversion lands here): the byte replacement is impossible, because moving the id would shift the FString length prefix in front of it and every offset after it. The save is parsed, the claims are rewritten through the real serializer, and the whole file is written back - which recomputes those prefixes. Everything the rewrite did not touch still round-trips byte-perfect.
Either way a file with no claim by the old id is left completely alone: no write, no .bak, no re-serialize.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.WorldSteamIdPatcher.PatchFile(System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Replaces every claim by with in . Returns the number of claims rewritten; the file is untouched (and no .bak written) when there are none.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.WorldSteamIdPatcher.PatchBytes(System.Byte[],System.String,System.String,System.Int32@)
member.summary: The in-memory form of , for callers that hold a world save's bytes rather than a file (packing a Game Pass container, above all). Returns the patched bytes and, via , how many claims changed; when nothing matched the input array is handed straight back so the caller can tell that there is nothing to write.
member.remarks: The different-length route parses as a world save, so only pass a WorldSave_*.sav here. Player saves carry no claims.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.WorldSaves.WorldSteamIdPatcher.PatchFolder(System.String,System.String,System.String)

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.Saves.SaveBackup
member.summary: Pre-write backups and crash-safe writes. Every editor write first copies the existing file to <name>.sav.bak (overwriting any earlier backup), then writes via a temp file and an atomic replace so a failure mid-serialize can never truncate or corrupt the live save. One backup level deep is enough to recover from a bad write while never growing unbounded.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.Saves.SaveBackup.CreateFor(System.String)
member.summary: Copies to <path>.bak (overwriting any earlier backup). A failed backup must not block the save itself, so this never throws; the return value lets callers report when no recoverable copy was made.
member.returns: True when a backup exists afterward, or the source did not exist (nothing to back up); false when the copy was attempted and failed.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.Saves.SaveBackup.WriteWithBackup(System.String,System.Action{System.IO.Stream})
member.summary: Backs up (best-effort) then writes new contents through into a sibling temp file and atomically replaces the target. If throws partway, the temp file is discarded and the live save is left exactly as it was - so a serialization failure can never leave a truncated/corrupt save behind, even when the backup could not be made.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.Saves.SaveDiscovery
member.summary: Finds every Abiotic Factor world installed on this machine, so the editor can offer them on startup instead of making the user hunt for folders. Four layouts exist: Steam/standalone client saves under %LOCALAPPDATA%\AbioticFactor\Saved\SaveGames\<account>\Worlds\<World>, Microsoft Store / Game Pass client saves under the packaged-app redirect %LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\<PackageFamilyName>\...\AbioticFactor\Saved\SaveGames\<account>\Worlds, Steam Play / Proton client saves (Linux, Steam Deck) inside a library's steamapps/compatdata/<appid>/pfx Wine prefix, and dedicated-server installs in Steam libraries, which keep their saves inside the install folder (a Worlds\<World> tree under any SaveGames directory). The per-account folder is treated as an opaque id, so non-Steam (non-numeric) owners list and load like any other.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.Saves.SaveDiscovery.DiscoverPackagedClientWorlds(System.String)
member.summary: Client-style worlds for a Microsoft Store / Game Pass install, whose packaged-app storage redirects %LOCALAPPDATA% into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\<PackageFamilyName>\.... The package family name isn't hard-coded (it can change across store releases), so this probes the standard UE-on-Store redirect subpaths under every package folder and, for any package whose name mentions Abiotic, searches a little deeper for a moved SaveGames tree. Each root found is handed to . Exposed for tests.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.Saves.SaveDiscovery.DiscoverProtonClientWorlds(System.String)

Each Proton game gets a Wine prefix at <library>/steamapps/compatdata/<appid>, and the game writes its usual AbioticFactor\Saved\SaveGames tree inside it. Every prefix is probed with the fixed sub-path (one cheap existence check each) instead of hard-coding the appid, so a beta or demo with its own appid is found too. Exposed for tests with an arbitrary library root.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.Saves.GvasTags
member.summary:
Shared low-level GVAS tag mutators used by the save writers. Everything operates on an existing tag found by prefix (property names carry blueprint-compiler hash suffixes), optionally creating a missing tag from its exact full hash-suffixed name.
Why creation is needed: Abiotic Factor delta-serializes - properties at their blueprint default are omitted from the file, so a prefix lookup can legitimately fail on a healthy save. Without creation the edit would silently no-op. New tags use , matching every game-written primitive tag observed in fixture saves.

member.summary: Replaces the contents of an existing Name/Str array property; no-op when absent.

Replaces a string array's contents. When the array is absent and is given it is created first, because the game delta-serializes an empty array away entirely: a world that has never unlocked anything simply has no such tag, and silently doing nothing there loses the edit.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.Diagnostics.EditorLog
member.summary:
Opt-in diagnostic logging for the editor. Disabled by default; when enabled, every call appends a line to %LOCALAPPDATA%\AbioticEditor\logs\editor-YYYYMMDD.log. One file per day, at most files kept (older ones deleted).
is the exception: errors are CRITICAL and always written, even when is false, so a failure is never silent just because a user left diagnostics off. // stay gated behind .
The logger must never take the app down: all of its own IO errors are swallowed. Writes are line-buffered (open/append/flush/close per line) so a crash loses at most the line being written, and the file is always readable while the app runs.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.Assets.AfInstallLocator.FindPaksDirectory
member.summary: Returns the absolute path to the game's Content/Paks directory, or null if the game can't be located. Resolution order: the explicit (in-process), then the environment variable, then the persisted choice (so a folder picked in the app is honored by the CLI and by a freshly launched app, even though the CLI never sets ), then Steam auto-detection. Each configured source is only used while it still resolves to paks, so a stale path falls through rather than disabling detection.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.Assets.BundledArt
member.summary:
The list of game pictures that were extracted ahead of time and shipped with the editor: skill icons, trader portraits, chapter cards, sector maps, creature and pet portraits, and the appearance previews. Item icons are NOT here - those are keyed by item id and handled separately (see the CLI's dump-icons).
This exists for the same reason does: the browser build cannot mount the game's pak archives, so anything it needs from them has to be dumped in advance. A host with the game installed ignores this entirely and extracts live.
It is only a list of names. Knowing WHICH pictures shipped is what lets a screen decide between drawing one and drawing its fallback symbol, without firing a request that 404s.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.Assets.GameDataRegistry
member.summary:
A pre-extracted snapshot of the game's data tables, dumped once from a real install (see the CLI's dump-registry command) and bundled in the editor's assets/ so the catalogs work with no game installed.
This is the generalization of the per-catalog hand-written Fallback tables (, TraderCatalog.Fallback, ...): instead of curating those by hand, the registry is generated from the paks and covers far more.
What it deliberately does NOT carry: icons/textures and fonts (binary pak assets), which still need the live install. The registry stores icon paths, so the editor shows names and stats offline and fills in icons only when the game is present.
Live pak data always wins when the game is installed (richer, with icons and DLC tables picked up automatically); the registry is the fallback, not a replacement.

member.summary: Bumped when the on-disk shape changes incompatibly; a mismatch is ignored, not loaded.
member.remarks: v2 added every catalog below . v1 carried items alone, which was enough for the desktop app (it reads the rest straight from the install) but left the browser build with no recipes, no codex, no traders, no skills and no appearance options at all.

member.summary: The cultures a dump ships for, in the game's own spelling. Kept as a list here rather than discovered at run time so a host can pick the right file with no wasted request: asking for a language that did not ship used to mean a 404 on every single page load.
member.remarks: Must match the files in assets/registry/; a test asserts the two agree, so a dump that adds or drops a language fails the build rather than silently mismatching.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.Assets.GameDataRegistry.BestCultureFor(System.String)

member.remarks: Exact match first, because the game ships some regional variants (pt-BR, es-419) and not their base language. Then any shipped culture with the same language, so de-AT gets German and pt-PT gets the Brazilian text rather than falling all the way back to English.

member.summary: Hands the registry to directly, for a host that cannot read it off disk. The browser build fetches it over HTTP at startup and calls this.
member.remarks: The alternative - writing the bytes into the in-memory file system WebAssembly provides and letting the normal path find them - looked simpler but failed silently: the registry never loaded, every catalog came back empty, and because that failure is only ever written to the log FILE there was nothing in the browser console to say so. member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.Assets.GameLocalizationLoader
member.summary: Primes CUE4Parse's Internationalization dictionary with Abiotic Factor's own shipped translations (the game's Content/Localization/Game/<culture>/Game.locres, one per supported language) so item/trait/skill/recipe display names resolve in a non-English culture.
member.remarks:
CUE4Parse's own requires AvailableCultures to be populated from DefaultGame.ini's CulturesToStage setting, which Abiotic Factor's cooked build does not set even though the locres files genuinely exist in the pak - a probe against the real install confirmed TryChangeCulture is rejected outright while the locres data itself parses fine and is extensive (50k+ translated strings for Russian). So this locates the culture's .locres files directly and feeds them to Internationalization via its public API, which FText resolution reads regardless of whether ChangeCulture "officially" succeeded.
Must run before any DataTable package is loaded: FText.Base.LocalizedString is resolved once, at deserialize time, not looked up live - so the culture has to be primed while the provider is still cold.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.Assets.ModTableDiscovery
member.summary:
Finds mod-added (and patch-added) DataTables across the mounted paks so every catalog can merge them without hardcoding the base content root. Discovery is keyed on the table's RowStructName: a mod that adds items/recipes/traits/etc. must reuse the game's row struct for the game itself to read the table, so struct identity catches mod tables regardless of their filename or content root (e.g. MyMod/Content/...).
The candidate set is restricted to assets named like a DataTable (the UE/AF convention, e.g. DT_*, CDT_*, ItemTable_*) so the scan does not have to load all ~50k mounted assets. A mod that ships a table under a non-conventional name will not be auto-discovered; its content simply degrades to raw ids, exactly as before this feature.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.Assets.WikiImageCache
member.summary:
Downloads images from abioticfactor.wiki.gg (via Special:FilePath/<FileName>, which 302-redirects to the actual file) and caches them under a local directory so every file is fetched at most once per machine. Lookups for an already-cached file never touch the network.
When the live wiki can't be reached (offline, 404, non-image response) the lookup falls back to a bundled copy shipped next to the executable (wiki\, see ) populated for the verified set by the CLI's download-wiki-images command. The live wiki is always tried first (so the picture stays current as the wiki is updated); the bundle is purely the offline safety net. A fallback hit is NOT copied into the per-machine cache, so a later online lookup still re-fetches the fresh wiki image. Only when neither the wiki nor the bundle has the file does the lookup return null and Warn-log once per file name.
Responses are validated by magic bytes (PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF); the cached file keeps the extension matching its actual format so image controls can load it.
Wiki content is CC BY-NC-SA - surfaces showing these images must carry the line.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.AbfSaveBundle
member.summary: Reads and writes the Game Pass ABF_SAVE_VERSION archive - the blob a world container holds. Layout: "ABF_SAVE_VERSION" marker, three header ints, a member count, a table-of-contents (path + uncompressed size + save class + flag per member), then one Oodle-compressed stream that decompresses to every member body concatenated in TOC order. Re-serialization is faithful for everything untouched; the Oodle bytes differ from the game's compressor but decompress to identical bytes, which is what the game reads.

member.summary:
Packs the Steam world folder at into a new Game Pass wgs container at . Returns the wgs folder path.
When is set a character is re-homed to that account id - the id in its file name and its SaveIdentifier, plus the beds it claimed - so it belongs to the target account. Leave it null to keep the existing ids. On a world with several characters say which one with ; the others are packed unchanged.
To re-home more than one character in the same run (a co-op world where several people are converting together), pass instead - a map of each character's current account id to the account it should belong to on the target platform. When given, it is used in place of /. A character left out of the map keeps its existing id, same as leaving both of those null.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassConverter.WouldStrandCharacters(AbioticEditor.Core.Saves.SavePlatform,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.String})
member.summary: True when converting this world without re-homing anybody would leave its characters owned by accounts the destination platform will never look for, so the game starts the player with a brand new character while their real one sits unopened in the folder.

remarks.para: The game finds a character by file name: Steam looks for Player_<SteamID64>.sav and Game Pass for the Xbox account's. A conversion carries every character across intact, but under the id it already had, so a world that changes platform without an account id given arrives complete and unreachable. This is what a player reports as "it made me a new level 1 character": nothing was lost, it is simply owned by the account they just left.

Only the cases that really bite say true. Heading for Steam, a character already on a SteamID64 is fine as it is. Heading for Game Pass, a SteamID64 is definitely not an Xbox account, while any other token might be, so only the certain mismatch is called out: a warning that cries wolf on a correct conversion is worse than none.

member.param: The platform the world is being converted to.
The world's character ids, from or .

member.name: F:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassConverter.EmptyRehomeMap
member.summary:
Works out which character a conversion is re-homing, or null when it is not re-homing one.
A shared world used to be refused outright, on the reasoning that one account id cannot own several characters. True, but the conclusion was wrong: the player only ever wanted their own character to become theirs on the new platform, and their friends' characters were never the target. Refusing meant a co-op world could not be moved at all - the game found no save for the player's account and offered character creation on top of a world they had 200 hours in. So several characters is fine as long as the caller says which one; only the ambiguity is refused, and the message lists the candidates so the answer is to hand.
member.exception: The choice is ambiguous, names a character the world does not have, or would collide with a character already on the target id.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassConverter.ResolveRehomeMap(System.Collections.Generic.List{System.String},System.String,System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyDictionary{System.String,System.String})

member.exception: An entry names a character the world does not have, or two characters would collide on the same destination account.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassDiscovery
member.summary:
Finds Abiotic Factor's Game Pass / Microsoft Store saves in the two places the Xbox "wgs" (Connected Storage) layout uses on PC:
the packaged-app redirect %LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\<PackageFamilyName>\SystemAppData\wgs\<XUID>_<...>\ (any package whose name mentions Abiotic, since the publisher hash varies), and
the per-drive game-save store <drive>:\XboxGames\GameSave\wgs\<XUID>_<...>\ which is shared across titles, so each container is checked for the Abiotic package name.
Never throws; inaccessible paths are skipped.

member.summary: Why a folder inside a wgs root is not a live save store, or null when it looks like one. Not everything in there is an account folder, and editing the wrong one is silent: the player's real save stays broken while the editor happily rewrites a copy of it.

remarks.para: The t folder is Connected Storage's own scratch area. On a live Abiotic Factor install it sits next to the account folder, holds no containers.index, and was empty every time it was looked at. It is named here rather than left to the no-index check so the log says what it is instead of implying something is wrong with it.

The rest are backup and copy shapes: this editor's own .bak snapshots (which stack up as .bak-<timestamp> and even .bak.bak), plus the naming other tools and the Xbox app are reported to leave behind.

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassWriteCheck
member.summary:
Everything the editor knows about whether a Game Pass save can safely be written right now.
Only two things are refused outright: a conflict Xbox has not settled, and a container in a state that makes it disposable (undefined, or a deletion tombstone). Both mean the save is already in an argument with the cloud before the player changes anything, and an edit written into one is settled later, out of sight, and can be settled against them.
The Xbox app and Gaming Services running is a warning rather than a refusal on purpose: on a Game Pass machine those processes are up essentially all the time (verified on a live install with the game closed), so refusing on them would refuse every edit forever, which teaches players to reach for the override on every save and makes it mean nothing.

A caller's explicit, recorded acceptance that a Game Pass save may be damaged or discarded by writing to it now.
Deliberately a token that has to be constructed by name rather than a bool force = false parameter: an argument like that is trivially passed by a caller who has not read what it means, and the failure it enables is silent and unrecoverable. member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassMemberCodec
member.summary:
Bridges a headerless Game Pass bundle member to a full GVAS save the editor can read, and back.
A Game Pass member is only the GVAS property body (it begins at the "unknown byte" that follows the save's custom header); the GVAS magic, versions, custom formats, class name and custom header are all stripped, with the save class recorded in the bundle TOC instead. To make the existing readers/writers work we prepend a class-matched header captured from a real save (); the body bytes are byte-identical, so the editor parses and re-serializes them faithfully. On write we strip the same-length header back off. The one field in that header that describes the body rather than the format - the custom header's data-length - is rewritten for the body actually being spliced on, because the captured template carries the length of the save it came from.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassMemberCodec.IsEditableSaveClass(System.String)
member.summary: True when a member of this save class is a GVAS save the editor understands.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassMemberCodec.DecodeIniText(System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Byte})
member.summary: Decodes the bundle's SandboxSettings.ini member to its real text. The game stores that member with every byte decremented by one (so [SandboxSettings] is written as ZR`mcanwRdsshmfr\); it is the only member that is not a GVAS body.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassMemberCodec.EncodeIniText(System.String)
member.summary: Re-encodes ini text into the shifted form the bundle stores (inverse of ).

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassMemberCodec.ToGvas(System.String,System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Byte})
member.summary: Reconstructs a full GVAS save from a headerless member body by prepending the class-matched header template and stamping the body's own length into the template's data-length field.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassMemberCodec.DataLengthOffset(System.String,System.Byte[])
member.summary: Where the data-length field sits in a header template: the last four bytes of the custom header, which is itself the last thing in the template. Located from the class name rather than assumed, so a template regenerated with anything extra on the end is rejected here instead of silently having four body bytes overwritten.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassMemberCodec.ToMemberBody(System.String,System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Byte})
member.summary: Strips a full GVAS save down to the headerless member body the bundle stores. The body begins at the "unknown byte" right after the save's custom header; that boundary is found by locating the save class name and skipping its fixed-size custom header, so it is correct for any save of the class (not only ones the editor just wrote with our header template).

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassWorldBackup
member.summary: The game's own spare copy of a world: the <World>-WC-B container that sits beside every <World>-WC in a Game Pass save.
member.remarks: Confirmed against a real 8-container Xbox save: the -WC-B container is a complete world bundle, not a fragment. It held all 70 members of its live twin (every region save, the metadata, all nine player saves and the world's SandboxSettings.ini) under the same world name, at an earlier generation - container.113 against container.170, with a slightly smaller Facility region. So it is a full, loadable rolling backup one generation behind, which is exactly what a player whose world has broken needs and could not previously see.

member.summary: High-level view of one Xbox "wgs" folder for Abiotic Factor: it surfaces the world/player saves packed inside each world container (<World>-WC) as virtual .sav files, hands the existing readers reconstructed GVAS bytes, and writes edits back through the bundle + wgs layers (Oodle recompress, new blob generation) with a one-time backup of the whole folder.

member.summary: World containers that failed to unpack the last time ran. They are skipped rather than aborting the whole folder (one broken world should not hide the others), but a caller that is about to act on "the world in this folder" must be able to tell the difference between a folder with one world and a folder where a second world failed to open.

member.summary: The parts of the save at that a repair would actually put right, answered without opening the world. Empty when there is nothing to repair.
member.remarks: Cheap on purpose: it reads the container list and checks which data files are present, and never unpacks a world. That is what lets a host ask the question BEFORE it opens a save, which is the only time the answer is any use. Asking afterwards leaves the player looking at a world that is already open, being offered the choice of opening it.

member.summary: Extracts every editable save in to as loose .sav files in the normal world layout (WorldSave_*.sav at the top, PlayerData/Player_*.sav underneath) so the standard folder editor can open them. Returns the world name. Works for one of the game's own backup containers () too, which is how a player gets an intact copy of a broken world out without restoring over anything.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassSaveSet.ApplyWorld(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Re-packs every edited save under (as laid out by ) back into in one pass: each member body is refreshed from disk, any staged player rename is applied, the bundle is Oodle-recompressed once, and a single new blob generation is written. Backs up the wgs folder on first write. Returns the number of members written.
member.exception: Not one member of the container was found in . That means the working copy is not the one this container was extracted to (moved, cleaned up, or renamed), and packing would write the container back unchanged - so the caller's save would silently do nothing. Failing here is what lets the host keep the edit and say so.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassSaveSet.StagePlayerRename(System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary:
Renames a player save inside 's bundle in memory, so re-homing a player to another account id survives the next repack. Nothing is written to the player's Xbox save until or runs, which keeps a rename part of the same SAVE as the edits around it instead of a separate write the player never asked for (and which would leave the container half-renamed if the save that followed it failed).
The rename has to reach the bundle at all because walks the bundle's own table of contents and looks on disk for each member's recorded name: a file renamed only in the working copy simply stops being found, and the container keeps the old player under the old id.
member.returns: True when a member was renamed.
member.exception: The new name is already taken in this bundle.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassSaveSet.RenamePlayerSave(System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Stages a player rename (see ) and immediately writes the container, for callers with no later save step of their own (the command line).
member.returns: True when a member was renamed and the container rewritten.

member.name: M:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassSaveSet.RenamePlayerToAccount(AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.GamePassSaveEntry,System.String)
member.summary: Re-homes a packed player save to and writes the container once. An owner id lives in two places - the save's file name and the SaveIdentifier inside it - and both are rewritten here in a single repack, so the container can never end up carrying a member named for one account whose contents claim another.

member.summary: Moves every claim held by the account named in over to across the container's world members, in memory. Returns how many changed; the caller repacks. member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.OodleCodec
member.summary:
Oodle (de)compression for the Game Pass ABF_SAVE_VERSION bundle payload. The bundle stores every world/player member as one Oodle-compressed stream (UE5's default codec), so the editor needs both directions: decompress to read, recompress to write. We P/Invoke OodleLZ_Decompress / OodleLZ_Compress directly on the native library.
The DLL is resolved lazily from, in order: the ABIOTIC_OODLE_DLL env var, the installed game's copy (next to its executable), a copy this codec previously downloaded and cached under %LOCALAPPDATA%/AbioticEditor/oodle, then CUE4Parse's downloader (the same mechanism the editor already uses for pak decompression) - that last step needs an internet connection but only ever runs once, since a successful download is cached for next time. When none can be obtained the codec throws so callers can degrade with a clear message rather than a crash.

member.name: F:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.OodleCodec.CacheDir
member.summary: Where a downloaded Oodle library is cached so later runs don't need internet again.

member.name: F:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.OodleCodec._downloadFailed
member.summary: Whether the one-off download has already been tried and failed this run. Without it every availability probe on an offline machine re-ran the download, inside , so each probe paid a fresh network timeout with every other caller blocked behind it - and, worse, two probes moments apart could disagree, because one caught a transient failure and the next caught a working retry. That made "is Oodle available?" non-deterministic within a single run. Only the network step is remembered: the cheap local lookups below still run every time, so setting ABIOTIC_OODLE_DLL or installing the game mid-session is still picked up.

member.name: P:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.OodleCodec.IsAvailable

member.name: T:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.WgsEntryState
member.summary: How Xbox Connected Storage tracks one container against its cloud copy.

remarks.para: Two reverse-engineering lineages disagree about 2, 4 and 5, and picking the wrong one writes a state that means something else entirely. This mapping follows libNOM.io (the engine behind the mainstream No Man's Sky editor) and is the one the evidence supports:

list.item: Across a real Abiotic Factor save and every backup of a live one, containers written by the game itself are only ever 1 or 2 - never 4 or 5 - and always carry an ETag.

Two independently written parsers (palworld-xgp-import, palworld-save-pal) reject any entry where state & 4 disagrees with "the ETag is empty". So bit 2 means local-only-never-uploaded, which 4 and 5 both are, and 2 cannot mean that.

remarks.para: The competing mapping (LukeFZ/XblContainerReader) calls 5 "Modified" and 2 "Unknown". Following it would have this editor stamp every edit as a container the cloud has never heard of while leaving an ETag on it - a combination no other tool produces, that those two parsers treat as corrupt, and that the Palworld tools found the sync engine silently discards.

member.summary: Changed locally since the last sync, and still based on a known cloud version - what a save this editor has just rewritten is. Keeps its ETag.

member.name: P:AbioticEditor.Core.GamePass.WgsContainer.StateContradictsEtag

Two independently written parsers reject an entry that breaks this, so producing one risks a save other tools - and plausibly Xbox itself - treat as damaged.
